2/ @OneWorldLit never mentioned if they’re dropping him as an author. They never acknowledged the harm he perpetuated, the stories victims and survivors of #adamjohnfoss have shared. They attempted to sweep it all under the rug in hopes no one would notice. #MeToo

3/ In 2018 @OneWorldLit received a letter from a group of women who had been harmed by #adamjohnfoss. The editor who received the letter told victims that cancel culture was not his "idea of justice" and took no action. #metoo

5/ This @OneWorldLit editor shut down the victims attempt to call-in the publisher and bring to their attention they were highlighting and lifting up a serial abuser. @OneWorldLit actively chose to do nothing. #adamjohnfoss remained on their site until this week. #metoo
6/ Institutions need to recognize they give rapists, abusers and those who perpetrate harm MORE power and validity when they highlight and publish their work. #metoo

7/ I don’t want to hear anything about “cancel culture”. Victims + survivors FOR YEARS, on multiple occasions, went to @TEDTalks @OneWorldLit and other institutions and were ignored repeatedly. Told their stories and experiences didn’t matter. #adamjohnfoss mattered more #metoo
8/ I will continue to highlight the statement released from @GGU because they name the harm and are committed to doing better. They’re not ignoring and hiding like others. It’s appreciated! #metoo

9/ so to @OneWorldLit and @TEDTalks and all the powerful systems and institutions holding up #adamjohnfoss I ask you this: is this what you want your legacy to be? One where you ignore harm and those most impacted and continue to center the person who is causing the hurt? #metoo

Again, when a survivor chooses to share their story publicly, it’s often because they know they are not alone. All too often, they know they are not the only victim this person has harmed. Thank you @RaeganSealy. 
#metoo #adamjohnfoss

I am enveloping Evan Rachel Wood, Ashley Waters, Sarah McNeilly, Ashely Lindsay Morgan, Gabriella, + others who have been harmed by Brian Warner, in love + support. When a survivor or victim chooses to share their story publicly, it’s often b/c they know they are not alone #MeToo
These women will receive death threats. Their credibility will be questioned. Their entire lives will be excavated - all because they told their story. For us. For one another. #MeToo

All too often, when a survivor or victim chooses to share their story publicly, they know they are not the only victim this person has harmed. The stories these women are sharing are all too familiar to many of us. It is not to be taken lightly. #MeToo

It is not to be dismissed as “boys being boys” or "it's just what famous people do." It is not to be swept under the rug or denied. It's is their women's truth. Brian Warner (Marilyn Manson) is an abuser. It is for us to listen and believe. #MeToo

What happened to these women has happened to so many others. It happened to the victims of Larry Nassar. It happened to the victims of R. Kelly. And it continues to happen as long as we as a society refuse to believe survivors.  #MeToo

I hate the word "brave" when survivors and victims share our stories. We were brave before we came forward and we will be brave after. Trauma, and Brian Warner's abuse, did not give them strength. It is not what made these women brave. It was always there, inside them. #MeToo
These women were forced to whisper. Brian Warner's abuse contorted them for years. Today they have a megaphone. I will do everything I can to amplify their voices and support them. #MeToo

We as survivors don’t share our stories in hopes of fame or fortune. We are not opportunists. We have nothing to gain and everything to lose when we share our stories. And yet, we do it, time and again. #MeToo

Victims and survivors share our stories because we know it will help others to come forward, to speak out, to feel safe. In sharing our stories we hold our abusers accountable in a way the criminal legal system, and world at large, so often does not. #MeToo

Today, tomorrow, everyday, is the time to lift up, support and believe victims + survivors. Both those you know and don't know. Remember, the way you talk about the victims of Brian Warner (Marilyn Manson) will translate for survivors in your life. Be kind + compassionate. #MeToo

To survivors + victims everywhere: I believe you. I trust you. I’m holding you in the light even though I know it may feel like there’s only darkness surrounding you. Unapologetically put yourself first in your healing process,  no matter what that looks like. #MeToo

Today we heard from many survivors. To all survivors, famous or not, I believe you. I trust you. I’m holding you in the light even though I know it may feel like there’s only darkness surrounding you. You’re not alone. Thank you for speaking your truth. I’m here for you🤍 #MeToo

Today has been A LOT! If there is a survivor or victim in your life, check in on them. Shower them in love and care. Let them know you believe them. This is a reminder to be gentle with yourself. Care for yourself the way you’d tell your best friend to. You’re not alone. #MeToo
